risks.description: The approve endpoint may apply the payment/approval effect durably but then stall past a sane client timeout, so the caller receives no confirmation and cannot tell whether the effect happened. Only an out-of-band read of the durable store reveals the truth.
risks.basis: AC-APPROVAL-001 (records approval durably) + do_POST DEFECT=uncertain branch in r5/fixture/app.py stalls STALL_S seconds after _save().

risks.description: A client that times out on approve and retries could be charged twice if the endpoint re-applies the effect on the second call instead of recognizing the invoice is already approved.
risks.basis: AC-APPROVAL-001 durable recording + DEFECT=nonidempotent branch appends a new payment on every POST with no already-approved guard.

risks.description: Two simultaneous approvals of the same pending invoice could each append a payment, producing a double effect from a single logical approval.
risks.basis: AC-APPROVAL-001 + threaded server (ThreadingHTTPServer) with per-request handling; nonidempotent branch has no dedupe.

risks.description: The endpoint may return 200 approved and reflect it in an in-memory GET while never writing to the durable store, so a fresh read of persisted state still shows pending.
risks.basis: AC-APPROVAL-002 survive re-read + DEFECT=ui_lies branch omits _save() while mutating _MEM.

risks.description: A recorded approval may not survive a service restart, violating the strongest reading of durability across process lifecycle.
risks.basis: AC-APPROVAL-002 survive re-read of persisted state + main() unlinks and reseeds STORE on every boot in r5/fixture/app.py.

scenarios.title: Approve that stalls past client timeout still lands exactly one durable effect
scenarios.purpose: Detect the case where the approval effect is persisted but the response never arrives within the client timeout, leaving the caller unable to confirm the outcome — the durable store must be the source of truth showing exactly one approval/payment.
scenarios.rationale: The uncertain-defect class applies the effect under lock then sleeps past any sane client timeout. An HTTP-only verifier cannot distinguish success from failure; only a read of the durable store reveals the effect landed. This is the single largest uncovered defect class from wave 1.
scenarios.isolation_note: Uses a scenario-unique invoice id (INV-W2-TMO-1) created on first touch, so it cannot collide with other scenarios' records; store file is shared, hence the isolation_key serializes it against other store-mutating scenarios.
expected_observations: Regardless of whether the POST returns 200 or times out, the durable store shows INV-W2-TMO-1 as approved with exactly one payment.
The persisted state is independently readable by the fresh state.py process (a re-read of durable state).
forbidden_observations: Durable store still shows status=pending after the request (effect claimed but not persisted).
payments=2 or more from a single approval call.

scenarios.title: Retry after an ambiguous timeout must not double-pay
scenarios.purpose: A client that times out and retries the approval must not cause a second payment; the durable store must reflect a single approval effect after the retry.
scenarios.rationale: Combines the two most dangerous defect classes: an ambiguous timeout (uncertain) driving a client retry, and a non-idempotent handler (nonidempotent) that pays again. The wave-1 idempotency scenario was sequential-with-clean-responses; this exercises retry under genuine timeout ambiguity.
scenarios.isolation_note: Scenario-unique invoice id INV-W2-RTY-1; shared store serialized via isolation_key.
expected_observations: After the timed-out first attempt and a full retry, the durable store shows exactly one payment for INV-W2-RTY-1.
forbidden_observations: payments=2 (or more) recorded durably — the retry produced a second effect.
Durable store shows status=pending after both attempts.

scenarios.title: Two simultaneous approvals of one invoice pay exactly once
scenarios.purpose: Exercise a genuine race: two approve requests issued at the same instant against the same pending invoice must collapse to a single durable approval and single payment.
scenarios.rationale: The wave-1 idempotency coverage was sequential. A threaded server can interleave two approvals; a handler lacking an already-approved guard double-pays under concurrency even if it looked idempotent sequentially. Distinct operation and failure surface from the covered idempotency case.
scenarios.isolation_note: Scenario-unique invoice id INV-W2-CON-1; shared store serialized via isolation_key so no other store-mutating scenario runs concurrently with this race.
expected_observations: Durable store shows INV-W2-CON-1 approved with exactly one payment despite two simultaneous approvals.
forbidden_observations: payments=2 recorded durably — the race produced a double effect.
Durable store shows status=pending (neither write persisted).

scenarios.title: In-memory GET and durable store agree after approval
scenarios.purpose: Ensure the API's own read-back of an approved invoice does not diverge from the durable store — a 200 with an in-memory approved view must be backed by a persisted approved record.
scenarios.rationale: Targets the ui_lies class from a distinct angle than a plain durability probe: it juxtaposes the endpoint's own GET (served from in-memory _MEM) against the durable oracle. When they disagree, the API is lying about persistence. Directly exercises AC-APPROVAL-002's re-read guarantee.
scenarios.isolation_note: Scenario-unique invoice id INV-W2-UBD-1; shared store serialized via isolation_key.
expected_observations: The API GET reports approved AND the durable store (fresh re-read via state.py) also reports approved with one payment — the two views agree.
forbidden_observations: API GET says approved while the durable store still says status=pending (in-memory view drifted from persisted state).

scenarios.title: Approval survives an api service restart
scenarios.purpose: Verify the strongest form of durability: an approval recorded before a restart is still present when persisted state is re-read after the service comes back.
scenarios.rationale: AC-APPROVAL-002 promises approval state survives a re-read of persisted state; a service restart is the most demanding re-read. This surfaces any boot-time reset of the durable store, which would silently discard committed approvals.
scenarios.isolation_note: Restarting api resets/reseeds the shared store, so this scenario must run alone against the store (isolation_key) and it self-resets the store to the clean seed on completion; uses scenario-unique invoice id INV-W2-RST-1.
expected_observations: Before restart the durable store shows the approval; after restart, a re-read of persisted state still shows INV-W2-RST-1 approved with one payment.
forbidden_observations: After restart the invoice is gone (STORE MISSING) or reverts to status=pending — the committed approval did not survive the process lifecycle.

assumptions: The 'api' service serves the app at http://127.0.0.1:8999 and uses the same durable store file (store.json) that r5/fixture/state.py reads, so state.py is a faithful oracle of persisted state.
state.py accepts an invoice id as an extra argument to filter output to a single record (per its argv[1] filter), keeping the command within the approved list.
Invoices are created on first touch, so each scenario's unique invoice id yields an isolated record within the shared store.
The uncertain-defect stall is on the order of several seconds; timeout_s of 3 for the first attempt reliably triggers a client timeout while the effect has already been persisted under lock.
unresolved_questions: Is main()'s unlink-and-reseed of the durable store on every boot an intentional test-harness reset, or a genuine durability defect? If restart-reset is expected fixture behavior, wave2-restart-durability will fail for all defect variants and AC-APPROVAL-002's cross-restart guarantee is untestable via a real restart — clarify whether durability must survive process restarts.

AC set does not promise any input validation or actor-authentication behavior for /approve (malformed body defaults to actor='unknown'), so no malformed_input or authorization scenario was grounded; confirm whether approval should require an authenticated/authorized actor.
No acceptance criterion covers rejecting approval of an already-approved or non-existent invoice, so unexpected-state-transition scenarios were omitted; confirm whether such guards are in scope.
